newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SAYS POSITION ON CABLE UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SAYS POSITION ON CABLE UNCHANGED.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday its position on its cable interests had not changed, despite a newspaper report it wanted to shed its cable television interests.

"There's nothing new happening," said a Philips spokeswoman. "We said at the third quarter results we would look at non-performing assets and of course we're looking over the portfolio of the media unit."
The Volkskrant newspaper said Philips wanted to dispose of its cable interests, which it said were worth 1.2 billion guilders, including those in Amsterdam, Eindhoven and Brussels.
Newly installed Philips chairman Cor Boonstra told reporters at the company's third quarter results announcement in October that he was tackling the company's problems aggressively.

"I will also take head on what I call the bleeders in the company, that means we will turn around, sell or close businesses that are not performing to our standards or are not fitting into our portfolio," he said then.

"There's a review of our assets and operations of course, that's what Mr. Boonstra said would happen," the spokeswoman said, declining to say whether the 1.2 billion guilder valuation for the cable interests was accurate.

Philips operates its cable television interests through the UPC joint venture with U.S. cable television firm United International . UPC is the biggest privately held cable firm in Europe with over two million connections and operations in 16 countries.
The cable interests are part of the Philips Media unit which in 1995 made an increased operating loss. A spokesman declined to give a breakdown of the division's figures.
"We do not wish to call cable a bleeder," he said, adding cable was a fast-growing, young industry that needed big investments but should be judged by its cash flow potential.

"It's a matter of looking at your assets from a strategic point of view. Do you want to keep cable or not? We've said we do not exclude any possibility, including a sale or a bourse flotation -- that's quite logical," the spokesman said.

Philips is a joint owner of the ill-fated Sport7 channel which last weekend went off the air after racking up at least 100 million guilders of losses in less than four months of operation. Other owners are PTT Nederland, ING and Dutch television producers John de Mol and Joop van den Ende.
